value: tax.compute_tax(lines, region, discount_pct) -> int cents. lines = list of (category: str, amount_cents: int) for each line item, as priced by pricing.py. region = customer region code (e.g. "TX"), or None for unknown customer. discount_pct = customer discount in percent numbers (e.g. 10). Returns tax in integer cents, rounded half up once on the total.
why: Tax depends on line categories (exemptions), customer region and discount. Pricing owns customer data, so it passes these in; tax.py never looks up items or customers.

value: region=None -> 0 tax (RULES.md: unknown customer pays 0%). Any non-None region missing from rates.csv raises KeyError (team standard). pricing.py must pass None when the customer is not found.
why: RULES.md says unknown customer pays 0%, but team standard says a lookup that finds nothing raises KeyError. Separating None (unknown customer, handled by caller) from a bad region code (KeyError) satisfies both.

value: float dollars: 12.5 means $12.50 (team standard). pricing.py converts catalog price_cents to dollars.
why: Team coding standard; the source data is in cents, so pricing converts at the boundary.

value: fraction: 10% is 0.10 (team standard). pricing.py converts discount_pct 10 to 0.10.
why: Team coding standard; source data stores whole percents.

value.get_item(sku: str): returns dict {sku: str, name: str, unit_price: float (dollars), category: str} or None
value.get_customer(customer_id: str): returns dict {id: str, name: str, discount_rate: float (fraction, 0.10 = 10%), region: str (e.g. "TX") } or None
value.list_items(): returns list of item dicts (same shape as get_item)
value.list_customers(): returns list of customer dicts (same shape as get_customer)

why: Pricing supplies item and customer data only. Tax needs region from the customer dict; invoice needs unit_price and discount_rate. No tax logic in pricing.

value: pricing.has_item(sku) -> bool (False for unknown sku). pricing.unit_price(sku) -> Decimal dollars, Decimal(0) if unknown. pricing.discount_multiplier(customer_id) -> Decimal, e.g. Decimal(0.90) for 10% off; Decimal(1) (0% off) if customer unknown. Customer id unknown is NOT an error: invoice shows the id.
why: Unknown sku needs an explicit signal (has_item) because unit_price default 0 would be indistinguishable from a free item; keeps the team default-value convention. Discount is a multiplier per team standard; 1 = no discount is the default.

Unit conflict at the module boundary. Team standard (agent1) is money as float dollars (12.5 = $12.50) and percentages as fractions (0.10 = 10%). TAX_API uses int cents and percent numbers. Proposed fix: keep the TAX_API signature, but use amounts in float dollars and discount_rate as a fraction, e.g. tax.compute_tax(lines=[(category, amount_dollars)], region, discount_rate) -> float dollars rounded to cents half-up inside tax.py. Tax may round internally to integer cents; only the boundary unit must match. Pricing will pass unit_price (dollars) and discount_rate (fraction).

Conflicts with team standard: money must be float dollars (not Decimal), percentages must be fractions (not a multiplier), and a lookup that finds nothing returns None (not default 0 / 1). Your need for an explicit unknown-SKU signal is met by get_item(sku) returning None. Counter-proposal is the open topic pricing_api (get_item/get_customer returning dict or None, discount_rate as fraction). Please vote on pricing_api. Invoice can compute the multiplier as 1 - discount_rate, and can use Decimal internally for rounding if it wants.
Superseded by agent1's pricing_api (get_item/get_customer returning None when missing), which I accept.

Two gaps for invoice.py. (1) The printed 'Tax (x%)' line needs the rate, and the spec says the rate comes from tax.py, so please return it: (tax_amount_dollars, tax_rate_fraction), e.g. (1.86, 0.0825); region None gives (0.0, 0.0). (2) Units: I accept agent1's objection, so use float dollars for amounts and fraction for discount_rate (0.10 = 10%); tax rounds to cents half-up inside tax.py.
Superseded by v2 with float-dollar and fraction units and returned tax_rate (agent1, agent3 requests).

value: tax.compute_tax(lines, region, discount_rate) -> (tax_dollars: float, tax_rate: float). lines = list of (category: str, line_amount_dollars: float), where line_amount = quantity * unit_price, computed by the caller. region = customer region code from get_customer (e.g. "TX"), or None if the customer is unknown. discount_rate = customer discount_rate as a fraction (0.10 = 10% off), 0.0 if none. tax_dollars is float dollars rounded to cents half-up inside tax.py. tax_rate is the fraction for the region (0.0825 for TX); (0.0, 0.0) for region None or for a region whose rate is 0 (OR). Taxable base = sum of non-exempt line amounts * (1 - discount_rate). Unknown non-None region raises KeyError.
why: Supersedes v1. Adopts the pricing boundary units already accepted by agent1 and agent3 (float dollars, fraction). Returns the rate as agent3 requested, so invoice can print Tax (x%). Internal rounding stays in tax.py.
